answer: Sybil resistance must price identity in exposed capital, not registrations. Each alias posts an umber-sized bond escrowed across epochs; an attacker mapping every alias onto one atlas of funding links exposes the whole cluster to coordinated slashing when any identity defects. Honest agents act as mirrors of each other's behaviour: attestors compare action histories, and a cluster whose echoes diverge from its declared stake forfeits the bond. Faking N identities costs N bonds plus the risk of the whole atlas collapsing, while honest agents risk only their own stake.
